text:
Assistant A answers all three parts of the question: it defines the central dogma, lists the processes (replication, transcription, translation) with explanations, and says Crick proposed it in 1958. Its wording ("proposed" and "first proposed by Crick in 1958") is accurate. Listing replication as part of the dogma is reasonable, since it is commonly included.

Assistant B is very brief. It defines the dogma and says Crick named it in 1958. It lists enzymes and ribosomes but never names the processes (replication, transcription, translation), so the second part of the question is only weakly addressed. Calling it "the process" is also slightly imprecise, and ribosomes are not enzymes in the usual sense.

A is more complete, more accurate, and more helpful.

[[A]]
